what_its_for: Ezetimibe is used to lower high cholesterol levels in your blood, specifically the 'bad' cholesterol (LDL). It works by blocking the absorption of cholesterol from the food you eat in your intestines. It is often used along with a healthy diet and sometimes combined with another cholesterol-lowering medicine called a statin.
how_to_take: Take ezetimibe by mouth, with or without food — it does not matter. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you are also taking a bile acid sequestrant medicine (such as cholestyramine or colestipol), take ezetimibe either 2 hours before or 4 hours after that medicine.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 10 mg tablet taken once a day. Always follow the dose your doctor has prescribed for you. Do not take more or less than what your doctor tells you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ezetimibe at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-fat or high-cholesterol foods while taking this medicine — your diet plays a big role in your treatment. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some can interact with ezetimibe. Limit alcohol consumption, as it may raise your triglyceride (fat) levels and can affect your liver.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or unusual tiredness); yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or very pale stools; stomach pain; severe allergic reaction signs such as rash, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or you have any concerns about your health.
when_it_works: Ezetimibe begins to lower your cholesterol within 2 weeks of starting treatment. Your doctor will likely check your cholesterol levels with a blood test after about 4 to 6 weeks to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel well, because high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Ezetimibe is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Children: Ezetimibe can be used in children aged 10 years and older, but only as directed by a doctor. Older adults (65+): No special dose adjustment is usually needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, ezetimibe may not be recommended for you. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
